decisions.decision: Rejected an external review's suggestion to set idleTimeoutMillis: 0 on the Prisma pg pool
decisions.rationale: Verified against pg-pool's actual source: 0 is falsy, so it skips setting up the idle-eviction timer entirely -- backwards from the intended fix, would have made dead-socket retention worse

decisions.decision: Retire Prisma connections after one use rather than tune timeouts further
decisions.rationale: Root cause of the dead-socket symptom is that Workers freezes the isolate (and the module-level pg pool) between requests; Supavisor drops the idle connection server-side during the freeze, and on wake the pool hands out a socket it believes is healthy. No client-side timer can catch this because timers are frozen too. One-use-then-retire sidesteps the whole class of bug instead of racing it.

decisions.decision: Kept Hyperdrive as the connection path (not a permanent direct-to-Supabase bypass)
decisions.rationale: Hyperdrive is still architecturally correct (edge pooling, query caching); the actual bug was a wrong port config, not Hyperdrive itself. A DB_BYPASS_HYPERDRIVE env var exists as a deliberate breaker switch for a future incident, not a default.
